scope: Proposition 14.2 (Uniform suppression near the two physical heights) of the manuscript “Signed cylinder propagation and marked polygons on the honeycomb lattice” (preprints/Signed-cylinder-propagation-and-marked-polygons-on-the-honeycomb-lattice-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2dda2109318f92bb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 113. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are constants 0 < δ0 < 1/16 and c1 > 0 with the following property. For every fixed discrepancy bound 0 ≤ C0 < ∞ there is n0(C0) such that, for integers n ≥ n0(C0), the conclusion below holds uniformly in f ∈ [0, 3/5]. Partition a list of n real heights into groups I0, I1 such that |I0| − n(1 − f) ≤ C0, |I1| − nf ≤ C0. Suppose |ha + f| < δ0 (a ∈ I0), |ha − (1 − f)| < δ0 (a ∈ I1). For every real x and every τ ∈ {P, O+, O−, U, L}, n Y a=1 ωτ (x; ha) ≤ exp  −c1ne−κ1|x|  , κ1 = π/3. (14.3) The sums of the one-site logarithms chosen to vanish at either infinity are O(ne−κ1|x|) there, uniformly in these lists. The proposition applies separately to each species.
